business_problem: Payload needed a database foundation for its developer-first CMS and application framework that could model dynamic content relationships, keep deployments simple, and outperform relational headless CMS competitors as usage grew.
solution_summary: Payload built its headless CMS and application framework around MongoDB so developers could work with a document model that fits dynamic content relationships instead of fighting relational constraints. MongoDB Atlas underpins Payload Cloud's one-click deployment path, giving the company a managed database option that stays fast under heavier website and application workloads, while MongoDB Community Edition remains available for customers who want to self-host on their own servers. The platform uses MongoDB documents to cross-reference content, create highly related entries, and render them into deliberate application experiences without extra translation layers. This architecture keeps the operational data model close to application code, simplifies deployment choices for customers, and gives Payload a strong base for future AI-oriented metadata and search features without leaving the same data platform.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Provides the managed database foundation for Payload Cloud's one-click deployments.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Community Edition
solution_components.role: Lets self-hosted Payload customers run the same document model on their own infrastructure.

data_flow: Content models, related entries, and application data created in Payload are stored as MongoDB documents, either in Atlas for Payload Cloud deployments or in Community Edition on customer-managed servers. Payload then reads those related documents back through its CMS and application framework to render websites and apps with deliberate, highly connected content.
business_outcome: Payload can deliver a faster, more flexible CMS platform, outperform key competitors in benchmark tests, and keep a simple MongoDB-based deployment path for both managed and self-hosted customers.
metrics: Running on MongoDB Atlas, Payload outperformed Strapi by 700% and Directus by 300%.
